layoutAssumptions: The existing project product illustration defines the visible silhouette: thick white base, continuous rear white sheet support, round-nose upper shelf, two black rings and left-side stored conoscope.
The project PDF, figures 2-2-9 and 2-2-10, supports the mechanical teaching relationship: base illumination, fixed lower polarizer, rotatable specimen support and rotatable upper analyzer.

Dimensions, bend radius, wall thickness, clear support, concealed attachments and material properties are not measured. Only necessary virtual support geometry is modeled; no hidden rear connector or internal wiring is invented.

The front oval amber window is based on the illustration only. Its identity conflicts with the PDF and earlier UI descriptions, so it is not identified as a power button; its glow follows the illustrative light state.
Conoscope is shown as a stored clear sphere in a hand-held ring; no focal length or quantitative optical prescription is claimed.
Exploded motion demonstrates component relationships, not a physical assembly or maintenance procedure.

source.history: The earlier v0.2 explored an existing project illustration; its master and provenance are preserved in archive-reference-v02. v0.3 introduced the independent twin-post layout and low base. In v0.3.1, direct user feedback led to a compact, thicker conventional box base, while retaining the independent frame and controls. The numeric dimensions remain our nominal teaching-design values. In v0.4, the user explicitly asked to use the original project instrument appearance and materials. The white folded support and visible body silhouette are therefore referenced again; the twin-post design remains only in revision history.
